rows.ARS:
Orange-pink Hybrid Tea.
Registration name: KORskipei
Exhibition name: Esther Geldenhuys
rows.Origin:
Bred by W. Kordes & Sons (Germany, 1987).
Introduced in South Africa by Ludwig's Roses as 'Esther Geldenhuys'.
rows.Bloom: Coral-pink. Moderate fragrance. 32 petals. Full (26-40 petals), borne mostly solitary, high-centered bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit: Tall, well-branched. Medium, glossy, medium green foliage.
rows.Growing: USDA zone 6b through 9b (default). Can be used for beds and borders, cut flower or garden. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that.
rows.Notes:
Dedicated to Esther Geldenhuys (ca. 1934 - June 28, 2012); South African rosarian
Zimbabwe patent application No. 8813 on April 25, 1988
